details:
Q1: How should the intake prove a reported run belongs to the claimed issue?
Choices:
A) Require all of these: the run is in `SOURCE_REPO`, its event is `issues` or `issue_comment`, its workflow path is that repo's clarify/plan/implement wrapper matching the `<phase>_failed` reason, its conclusion is `failure`, and the claimed issue has a phase-failure comment from the workflow account that links that exact run URL. The comment is the same evidence `phase_failure_streak` already counts. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Check repository, workflow path, event and conclusion only. Skip the issue link, so a forged report could still point at a real failed run that belongs to another issue.
C) Same as B, plus require the run's `display_title` to match the issue title. This is weaker than A because titles are not unique and can be edited.
Q2: What should happen when verification fails or the GitHub API can't answer (the run is unreadable, comments can't be fetched, or there is a mismatch)?
Choices:
A) Fail closed: drop the report with a stable `WORKFLOW_HEAL ... outcome=skip reason=phase_report_unverified` log line and a Telegram WARNING. No heal issue is filed and no lineage is escalated. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Fail closed only on a confirmed mismatch. If the API is unavailable, process the report as today.
C) Process the report but tag the heal issue "unverified provenance" and never escalate it on that report.
Q3: How should "bind each reporter credential to its authorized source repository" be handled? A `repository_dispatch` only exposes `sender`, and consumers typically dispatch with the same owner's `GH_PAT`.
Choices:
A) Use the Q1 checks as the binding. The intake reads the run, issue and comments in the claimed `SOURCE_REPO` with its own token, so a forged report can't reference evidence outside that repo. Leave per-credential binding out of scope and say so in the PR. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Also add an optional per-repo allowed-`sender` list next to `.github/ai/consumer_repos.json`, in a new file so the existing array format stays unchanged. Reports from a repo with a configured list must match it.
C) Change `.github/ai/consumer_repos.json` entries to objects with an allowed sender. **Note:** this changes the format of a file the release dispatch reads, which is a breaking change.
Q4: Which report kinds should get the new provenance check?
Choices:
A) `phase_failure` only, as the finding cites. (RECOMMENDED)
B) `phase_failure` plus `autofix_failure`, which also builds run references from reporter-supplied run IDs. This also needs a check that the run belongs to the PR.
C) Every kind that carries `run_refs`, including `workflow_run`.
